title: Weil and polarization input for determinant signs
as_he_states: The weight and sign formulas are conditional on Weil/standard conjectures and an admitted selfduality.
plausible_today: For rational pure geometric Frobenius data with a specified alternating polarization, parity and positive normalized determinant follow; arbitrary pure sheaves need not be selfdual.
state_of_art: Deligne1974 Theorem1.6 and §2.6; Deligne1980 §§1.8,3.3 establish precise weights. They do not prove every standard conjecture or construct a polarization on every proposed motive.
why_open: The pages explicitly admit inputs; no reason for a later abandonment is documented.
worth: Worth a short hypothesis audit, since separating purity, rationality and polarization prevents false counterexamples.

title: Generic selfduality and extension
as_he_states: Selfduality is admitted, with a compressed generic-point remark whose ink is uncertain.
plausible_today: A given generic isomorphism of lisse sheaves on a normal integral scheme extends uniquely; its existence remains separate.
state_of_art: Stacks0BQM gives the required fundamental-group surjectivity.
why_open: The text does not explain whether the generic existence is assumed or claimed; no external source resolves the handwriting.
worth: Worth resolving on the scans before attaching a universal motivic assertion.

title: Boundary type and weight bound
as_he_states: With resolution and Weil conjectures, the boundary has the proposed lower type and indicated weights.
plausible_today: Precise cohomological weights can be stated for mixed lisse sheaves; a type bound requires a definition of the source type predicate.
state_of_art: Deligne1980 §§3.3–3.4 supplies weight inequalities. Wildeshaus Theorem6.1 supplies a distinct motivic boundary duality under resolution. Neither identifies the undefined type.
why_open: The source leaves its invariant unspecified here, rather than presenting a complete theorem.
worth: Worth an archival definition search; a theorem search alone cannot recover the missing predicate.

title: One-unit boundary duality shift

title: Variation of Euler characteristic and determinant
as_he_states: A margin asks for variation with E and X or n.
plausible_today: Specify a geometric family or coefficient operation; base-field extension sends F to F^r, χ to χ and δ to δ^r, while exact sequences give determinant multiplicativity.
state_of_art: The elementary base-extension and exact-sequence cases are proved here; the curve local-constant product gives a more structured variation framework after fixing its data.
why_open: The margin contains a direction rather than hypotheses or a proposed conclusion.
worth: Worth developing only after choosing a family; one short run can compare tame rank-one twists and conductor jumps.

title: Repairing the nonadditive generic extension
as_he_states: The ordinary extension L* is reproached for nonadditivity; a global composition-factor construction is then rejected as insufficiently local and incompatible with étale extension.
plausible_today: Use the local decomposition group, normal unipotent subgroup and exact finite-group averaging on K₀; retain ordinary invariants as a different functor.
state_of_art: Deligne1973 §8 supplies the local quasi-unipotent/Weil–Deligne context. The handwritten averaging argument is independently checked.
why_open: The text itself gives the reason for rejecting the first recipe: locality and étale compatibility.
worth: Worth a short categorical comparison; no claim that the first global recipe already has the needed functoriality should survive.

title: Geometric local factors and absolute values
as_he_states: Problem(a): determine local α, μ, λ and characteristic polynomials, especially Frobenius absolute values, in geometric situations.
plausible_today: For a specified pure lisse sheaf on a curve over a finite field, use the monodromy filtration and local weights; α is computed from inertia and μ vanishes in the stated category.
state_of_art: Deligne1980 Theorem1.8.4 and Remark1.8.8 give the precise local purity theorem. Averaging alone does not compute the representation.
why_open: The question asks for geometric information not supplied by the preceding formal construction.
worth: Worth a bounded worked degeneration example, starting with semistable rank two and finite tame inertia.

title: Computing the modified Euler characteristic
as_he_states: Problem(b) asks for χ; scan59 points to Artin representations.
plausible_today: GOS plus the degree-weighted dimensions of the averaged stalks computes χ♮ on a smooth proper curve with a lisse open restriction.
state_of_art: Raynaud1965 §3 Theorem1, published1966, gives Grothendieck’s formula; Laumon1987(3.1.5.3) gives the conductor form.
why_open: The pages give a reference direction, not a full calculation.
worth: Resolved in the stated curve setting; a useful next task is a convention-complete example with closed points of degree greater than one.

title: Global determinant from local data, including its sign
as_he_states: Problem(c) asks to calculate δ; the following calculation reaches only a result modulo sign.
plausible_today: Fix additive character, differential and geometric Frobenius conventions, then express the global epsilon constant as a product of local constants.
state_of_art: Deligne1973 Theorem4.1 gives local constants; Laumon1987 Theorem3.2.1.1 proves the curve product formula for constructible complexes.
why_open: The manuscript explicitly says “modulo un signe”; the needed later local data are not specified here.
worth: Worth a short translation of one example into Deligne–Laumon conventions; the general product theorem is established.

title: Questioned square of the normalized determinant
as_he_states: A circled question asks whether δ♮²=q^χ♮; later formulas introduce local factors.
plausible_today: The square includes the local defect determinant product; after μ cancellation it simplifies in the stated category, but a square never determines its root sign.
state_of_art: Independent determinant derivation in proof_notes.md and CALC-09; the sign-sensitive replacement is the Laumon product theorem with extra data.
why_open: The question is visibly followed by a more elaborate calculation; one intermediate factor is inconsistent and needs scan review.
worth: Worth a source-focused normalization audit; the elementary square identity itself is now checked.

title: Strict lower-niveau normalization
as_he_states: Find λ of strictly smaller niveau making σ(λL)/(λL) a constant sign; revise the initial weight-range description using structured factors.
plausible_today: For a precisely specified σ-stable multiplicative subgroup H of allowed factors, ask whether the norm-one multiplier is a coboundary in H; fixed-point order parities give necessary tests.
state_of_art: Unrestricted solutions are elementary and explicitly computed. Targeted archive, arXiv, zbMATH and MathOverflow searches did not identify a theorem with the page’s undefined H or niveau.
why_open: The text rejects the trivial λ=1/L and changes its allowed-factor language; the exact restriction remains insufficiently defined in the supplied fragment.
worth: High interest after archival clarification; one few-hour run can classify a finite divisor-support model, not solve an undefined general programme.

title: Haar uniqueness deferred to another chapter
as_he_states: The reused printed text invokes uniqueness of Haar measure and refers the proof elsewhere.
plausible_today: Every locally compact group has a nonzero left Haar measure, unique up to positive scalar.
state_of_art: Alfsen1963 proves existence and uniqueness; its covering ratios and approximate-additivity Proposition1.1 match the relevant mechanism, but its constructive proof is different from the draft’s ultrafilter step.
why_open: This is an editorial cross-reference in printed Bourbaki material, not a stated doubt of the handwritten author.
worth: No new mathematical development is needed; locating the draft chapter counterpart would improve provenance.
